one_line: An 8.5-second teaser: a staged family of four on a sofa with popcorn buckets under a 'classic movies for family movie night' caption, with a Notion-style checklist of films by decade scrolling too fast to read, and the full printable gated behind a 'Comment 100' keyword in the caption.

hook.visual: Static front-on shot of two adults and two small children on a dark sofa; both kids hold popcorn buckets and the adults lean in. Grey wall behind with a 'KEEP CALM AND CARRY ON' style poster. Nothing moves much for the first 2 s until a white checklist card appears over the lower half.
hook.on_screen_text: Here's all the classic movies you need for family movie night... (English on screen; no translation needed)
hook.first_spoken_line: Can I stay a bit longer? (Whisper transcript at 0-2 s; no visible speaker, so source of the line is unverified)
hook.why_it_stops_the_scroll: Inferred: a cosy, familiar scene (family, popcorn, sofa) plus a promise of a complete answer to a recurring parent question ('what do we watch tonight'), then a white list card lands at 2 s so the viewer sees the promise being delivered at once.

beats.observed: Staged family on a sofa eating popcorn from two buckets; the caption pill (white text on a black rounded box) is already on screen and stays there for the entire 8.5 s.
beats.spoken: Whisper: 'Can I stay a bit longer?' at 0-2 s. No lip movement visible on a speaker; could be a track layered over the clip (inferred, unverified).
beats.on_screen_text: Here's all the classic movies you need for family movie night...

beats.observed: A white checklist card with round check circles appears over the lower half of the frame: header '🎥🍿 Family Movies 🍿🎥', section 'Golden Age / Mid-Century Classics', 15 titles from 'The Wizard of Oz (1939)' to 'The Sound of Music (1965)'.
beats.spoken: Transcript has no speech between about 2.0 and 4.7 s.
beats.on_screen_text: Family Movies | Golden Age / Mid-Century Classics | The Wizard of Oz (1939) ... The Sound of Music (1965)

beats.observed: The card is now scrolled: '1970s Classics' (5 titles incl. Willy Wonka & the Chocolate Factory (1971), Star Wars: A New Hope (1977)), '1980s Classics' (8 titles incl. E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial (1982), Back to the Future (1985)), top of '1990s Modern Classics' (Toy Story (1995), Matilda (1996)). The 3 s and 4 s frames look identical.
beats.spoken: Whisper: 'Stay forever.' at about 4.7-6.7 s (unverified source).

beats.observed: Scroll continues through '1990s Modern Classics' (to The Iron Giant (1999)) and '1990s Family-Friendly Classics' (Home Alone (1990) to Balto (1995)), then the end of that block (The Lion King (1994) ... Mulan (1998)) and the start of 'Early 2000s (Now Considered Classics)'.
beats.spoken: Whisper: 'Stay forever.' continues to about 6.7 s.

beats.observed: The list lands at the top of the 'Early 2000s' section and ends at 'Up (2009)'; a red spell-check underline is visible under 'Terabithia' in 'Bridge to Terabithia (2007)', which suggests a live editable document was screen-recorded rather than a designed graphic (inferred).
beats.on_screen_text: Early 2000s (Now Considered Classics) | Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone (2001) ... Up (2009)

payoff: The list is visible from 2.0 s, but it scrolls through dozens of titles in about 6 s so it cannot be read; the real payoff (the full '100 Best Family Movies' printable) is only available by commenting '100' as the caption says.
cta: Caption only: 'Comment 100 to download our free resource: 100 Best Family Movies'. No CTA appears on screen or in the transcript.
share_or_comment_trigger: Utility plus gate: a parent can't read the list in the video, wants it, and the only route is typing '100'. Also sendable to a partner ('movie night this weekend?'). Comments (3,339) are about a third as many as likes (10,377), which is a gate-driven pattern rather than a conversation.
why_it_worked: 8.5 s is short enough to finish and replay, and the list scroll rewards a replay or a pause (inferred; no retention data in meta.json); 1.21M views is 10.3x the account median of 117,551.

Comment gate on a free printable: 3,339 comments is 0.27% of views and about 32 comments per 100 likes, versus about 0.7 per 100 likes on the story reel in this batch, so most comments are probably keyword requests (inferred).
Search-intent topic with a one-line promise ('all the classic movies you need'); the list shown in decade chunks looks complete and save-worthy at a glance.
paid_signal: unclear: like_rate_pct 0.85 is above the 0.3 paid pattern and the high comment count is explained by the keyword gate, so no direct sign of promotion, but nothing rules it out.

solo_route.how: 1) Build a free resource in Notion or Canva with the same chunked layout and circle checkboxes (for example 'moments worth turning into a book, by age'), plus a PDF version as the download. 2) Screen-record the page scrolling on a phone, speed it up so it cannot be read in about 6 s. 3) In CapCut put it over a licensed stock clip of a family on a sofa (Pexels or Canva) or an AI-generated cosy family clip, add the single caption pill for the full 8 to 9 s, and trim it to about 8 s. 4) In the caption write 'Comment [keyword] to download' and set an auto-reply DM with the PDF link.
solo_route.needs: The actual checklist PDF or page to give away; a comment-to-DM tool; a stock licence or an AI clip. No filming, no child and no permission needed.

lumebook_version.hook_he: 40 רגעים של הילד שכדאי להפוך לספר. הרשימה המלאה בתגובות
lumebook_version.concept: An 8 second teaser over a stock or AI family-on-sofa clip with a scrolling Notion-style checklist of milestone moments by age (first steps, first day at gan, lost first tooth, and so on). Viewers comment a keyword to get the PDF, which ends with a LumeBook free preview offer.

evidence_notes: Observed: both sheets (0 to 8 s) and single frames at 0, 2, 3 and 8 s; all list titles quoted come from frames and are readable at frame size, but I did not count the full list, and the 100-title claim comes only from the caption. Spoken: whisper.srt has two short lines ('Can I stay a bit longer?' 0-2 s and 'Stay forever.' about 4.7-6.7 s); no visible speaker matches them, so they may be a background audio track and are unverified. Made-by judgement is inferred: no creator handle, credit or collab tag is visible in the frames or caption, the family footage looks like polished stock (inferred) and the account is a brand, so this is treated as in-house editing of licensed footage rather than a repost of a creator's clip, but the footage source is unverified. The Notion-style look and spell-check underline are inferences from the frames.
